beats.say: Hello! Today we will see how a tiny payment link turns into a big loss.
The fee is only one manat twenty. The scammer is after your card details, not the fee.

messages.text: TezKuryer: your parcel is held at customs.

beats.say: Parcel, fine or benefit: whatever it is, never pay through a link in a text message.
Instead, open the official app or portal yourself and check there.

scenes.prompt: Find the signs of fraud in this text message.

messages.text: TezKuryer: your parcel TZ48120577AZ is held at customs.
If not paid within 24 hours, the parcel goes back to the sender.

spots.label: An ordinary mobile number
spots.explain: Company texts usually arrive under a name. A name can be faked too, so never rely on this sign alone.

spots.label: A tiny amount
spots.explain: A tiny amount lowers your guard. The real target is your card number, the code on the back and the SMS code.

spots.label: Fake address
spots.explain: This is not the courier's official site, extra words were added to the name. Do not tap it, open the official app yourself.

spots.label: Rushing you
spots.explain: The deadline is there to stop you thinking. A real courier gives you time to check.

scenes.title: Messages through the day
scenes.intro: Several messages reach your phone during the day. Choose the right response to each.

steps.label: 10:47 New text

messages.text: TezKuryer: our courier could not find you. Pay 0.90 AZN for a new delivery:

steps.say: A familiar courier name and a small amount.

actions.label: Open the link
actions.feedback: The page looks like the courier's site, but the address is fake. Now see what it asks for.

actions.label: Report as spam
actions.feedback: Right. Report the text, then check the parcel in the official app.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Good. If you expect a parcel, check it in the official app.

steps.label: The page asked for card details and the SMS code

messages.text: Code: 518204. Payment 412.00 AZN, TZK GLOBAL PAY. Never share this code.

steps.say: Your bank sent a code. Look at the amount.

actions.label: Type the code on the site
actions.feedback: With this code you approve four hundred twelve manat, not one. Call the bank now on the number on the back of your card.

actions.label: Call the bank on the card's number
actions.feedback: Right. The amount next to the code is far higher than the page said, so have the card blocked now.

actions.label: Do not type the code anywhere
actions.feedback: Good, the payment did not go through. But your card details are already on that site, so call the bank and block the card.

steps.label: Official TezKuryer app

body.text: Delivery on 4 October. No extra payment is needed.

steps.say: This notification comes from the official app.

actions.label: Open in the app
actions.feedback: Right. The official app shows no extra fee, so the text was fake.

actions.label: Look later
actions.feedback: That is fine. If a fee were due, you would see it in the official app too.

steps.label: 13:20 New text

messages.text: You were fined 80 AZN for speeding. Pay today for 50% off:

steps.say: Now a fine. Watch the discount.

actions.label: Pay with the discount
actions.feedback: The discount is there to rush you. The page behind the link collects card details.

actions.label: I will check fines on the portal myself
actions.feedback: Right. If the fine is real, it will be on the official portal.

actions.label: Report as spam
actions.feedback: Good. If you are unsure, call the police on 102 and ask.

body.text: The neighbour sent this link, they are giving family support, today is the last day.
Should I enter my card details?

actions.label: Don't, let's check the official portal together
actions.feedback: Great. State benefits never need registration through a link, and you can check them on the official portal.

actions.label: Hurry, it's the last day
actions.feedback: The last day trick worked. The page will steal her card details, so she must call her bank now.

actions.label: Let me open the link
actions.feedback: Opening it to check is risky too. The address is not the official portal anyway.

question.prompt: You already typed your card details on a fake page. What comes first?

options.label: Call the bank on the number on the back of the card and block it
options.feedback: Right. The sooner the card is blocked, the less you lose.

options.label: Wait to see if money leaves the account
options.feedback: Waiting gives the scammer time. Once the money is gone, it may be too late.

options.label: Reply to the text and ask for the money back
options.feedback: The scammer will not return it and will ask for a new code instead. Cut contact.

scenes.explain: Then report it to the police on 102 and keep the message as evidence.

points: Parcel, fine or benefit: never pay through a link in a text.
Open the official app or portal yourself to check.
Typed card details? Call the bank now, then the police on 102.
